content_voiceover: This table is a board favorite, matching membrane proteins to their disease phenotypes. Ankyrin defects are the most common cause of typical dominant hereditary spherocytosis. Band 3 defects cause HS, but also Southeast Asian ovalocytosis, nonimmune hydrops fetalis, and hereditary acanthocytosis, band 3 HS classically shows pincered spherocytes on the blood film before splenectomy, and SAO results from a specific 9 amino acid deletion. Alpha spectrin defects cause HS, HE, hereditary pyropoikilocytosis, and NIHF, with acanthocytic spherocytes on film, and here the location of the mutation determines the clinical phenotype. Beta spectrin is the most common cause of typical HE, but also causes HS, HPP, and NIHF. Protein 4.2 deficiency causes HS and is notably enriched in Japanese patients with autosomal recessive inheritance, a classic board pearl. Protein 4.1R deficiency causes HE and is found in certain European and Arab populations, and glycophorin C defects cause HE through concomitant protein 4.1 deficiency. High yield associations to memorize, ankyrin and protein 4.2 for HS, especially the Japanese autosomal recessive protein 4.2 link, and beta spectrin for HE.
keypoints: Ankyrin = most common cause of dominant HS
Protein 4.2 deficiency → HS, AR, classic in Japanese patients
β-spectrin mutations = most common cause of typical HE
Band 3 → HS (pincered cells), SAO (9-aa deletion), NIHF, HAc
keypoint_voiceover: Key protein-disease pairs for boards, ankyrin is the most common cause of dominant hereditary spherocytosis, and protein 4.2 deficiency, causing HS, is classically autosomal recessive and enriched in Japanese patients. Beta spectrin mutations are the most common cause of typical hereditary elliptocytosis. Band 3 defects give you pincered spherocytes in HS, and also cause Southeast Asian ovalocytosis from a 9 amino acid deletion. And remember, alpha spectrin's phenotype depends on exactly where the mutation sits.
